::: {#brief .lx-sec}
```{=html}
<div class="lx-card lx-sb-brief">
<p class="lx-eyebrow">The brief</p>
<dl class="lx-sb-facts">
<div><dt>The site</dt><dd>Prairie Campus (fictional, from <a href="f07-microgrids.html">F7</a>): a county hospital, a water and heating plant, dorms and labs, <b>1,200 kW</b> in all, on one feeder.</dd></div>
<div><dt>You decide</dt><dd>What must stay on; solar (kW), battery (kWh), 200 kW generator sets and diesel (gallons); the feeder's limits, the tariff and the owner.</dd></div>
<div><dt>The engine works out</dt><dd>A normal year on the grid, then each outage hour by hour as an island; or the cheapest sizes, with a small <span class="lx-term" data-term="mixed-integer-program">mixed-integer program</span>.</dd></div>
<div><dt>It leaves out</dt><dd>Prices (a mixed-integer program gives none), the wiring inside the campus, part-load fuel use, battery wear, and outages you do not choose.</dd></div>
</dl>
<p class="lx-hint">Open-ended: start from a preset, change one thing at a time, and copy the plan link to keep a plan.</p>
</div>
```
:::

::: {#explain .lx-sec}
::: {.lx-sec-h}
## How the engine works, as diagrams
:::

```{=html}
<div id="sb1-explain" class="lx-xgrid">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<dl class="lx-ideas">
<dt>Run the outages</dt><dd>A linear program runs a normal year on 12 average days; then a mixed-integer program runs each outage as an island, with whole 200 kW sets that run at 30% or more.</dd>
<dt>Size it for me</dt><dd>One mixed-integer program picks the cheapest solar, battery and whole sets that keep every must-stay-on load on in every chosen outage; the run then checks them.</dd>
<dt>It holds when</dt><dd>The chosen outages are the ones that matter, loads are flat, and the coming sun is known.</dd>
<dt>It leaves out</dt><dd>Prices, the campus's wiring, part-load fuel use, battery wear, fuel deliveries, and how often outages happen.</dd>
</dl>
</div>
</div>
```

```{=html}
<div class="lx-deepers">
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Modeler</span>The model behind the bench</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

[M5](m05-microgrid-size-and-run.html) writes the engine down: the decisions, the cost and every rule, proves the sizing with a branch-and-bound tree, and runs the storm on forecasts with a rolling horizon. Its notebook rebuilds the same models in Python and checks the bench's numbers.

```{=html}
</div>
</details>
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper</span>How the outages are chosen</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

The three named outages are real 2025 stretches of sun with the grid assumed down: 72 hours from 00:00 on 20 January, 24 hours from 16:00 on 20 January, and 72 hours from 00:00 on 28 July. The ten drawn outages use seed 7: each starts at a whole hour from 1 January to 25 February 2025, every hour equally likely, and lasts 6 to 72 hours, every length equally likely. They are a teaching sample, not outage statistics: a plan that rides through all ten has passed ten tests, nothing more.

```{=html}
</div>
</details>
</div>
```
